title: Video & Screenshot Uploader for ClickUp — record, annotate, attach
description: Free, open-source Chrome and Firefox extension: record your screen or annotate a screenshot, then attach it to a new or existing ClickUp task, or save the recording to your ClickUp Clips, from the browser's side panel. Uses your own ClickUp token; talks to ClickUp and nothing else.

sections.heading: Three steps, one panel. Or one tab for Clips.
sections.text: Three steps, one panel. Or one tab for Clips. Everything happens in the browser's side panel, next to the page you're looking at. Capture Record a clip of your screen, a window or a tab. Or take a screenshot of the visible tab, a dragged-out area or the whole screen, then draw, write, blur and crop before anyone sees it. Describe Pick the list, give the task a title and a formatted description (bold, lists, checklists, links, code), set status and priority. sections.heading: Everything it does
sections.text: Everything it does Built for people who file bugs and feedback all day: QA, support, designers, product folks. Screen recording Your entire screen, a window or a tab, at 720p up to 4K or native size, with any microphone and system audio. Add yourself as a movable camera bubble if you like. Clips are written to disk as they record, so long ones don't fill memory. In Chrome you can close the panel while it records. sections.heading: Chrome and Firefox
sections.text: Chrome and Firefox The same panel in both. A few things differ because the browsers do. Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi Firefox Where the panel lives Side panel Sidebar Record a single tab Yes Screens and windows only System audio in recordings Yes, tick "Share audio" in the picker Microphone only Recording while the panel is closed Yes, a REC badge shows it's running Keep the sidebar open and stop from it. If it's closed, what was recorded is kept Minimum version Chrome 123 Firefox 128

sections.heading: What it does with your data
sections.text: What it does with your data Everything stays in your browser until you press Create, Upload or Save to Clips. Data goes to one place: ClickUp. Its API with your own token, and ClickUp's own web app, with your sign-in, only for the Clips tab. The developer runs no servers for this extension and receives none of your data. No analytics or tracking in the extension. Nothing is sold. The full privacy policy lists every piece of data the extension touches and why.
